subject: Chemistry
title: Crystal Field Theory (CFT): Octahedral (Δ_o) vs. Tetrahedral (Δ_t)
topics: Crystal Field Theory (CFT) Foundations: Electrostatic Point-Charge Model (Bethe & van Vleck)
6.1 Octahedral Splitting (Δ_o): e_g Doublet (+0.6 Δ_o / +6 Dq) vs t_2g Triplet (-0.4 Δ_o / -4 Dq)
Cartesian Axis Approach of Ligands (x, y, z) & Direct vs Inter-Axial Orbital Repulsion
6.2 Tetrahedral Splitting (Δ_t): t_2 (+0.4 Δ_t) vs e (-0.6 Δ_t)
High-Spin Rule for Tetrahedral Complexes (Δ_t << P enforces high-spin)
quickSummary: CFT treats metal-ligand bonds as purely electrostatic point charges. In octahedral fields, d-orbitals split into higher e_g doublet (+0.6 Δ_o) and lower t_2g triplet (-0.4 Δ_o). In tetrahedral fields, splitting is inverted: higher t_2 (+0.4 Δ_t) and lower e (-0.6 Δ_t). Δ_t = (4/9) Δ_o. Because Δ_t << P, tetrahedral complexes are almost always high-spin.
summary: Master Octahedral and Tetrahedral crystal field splitting patterns, orbital energy shifts, and the Δ_t = (4/9) Δ_o relationship.

summaryBox.title: Octahedral Field Splitting
summaryBox.takeaway: e_g doublet (d_x²-y², d_z²) raised by +0.6 Δ_o (+6 Dq). t_2g triplet (d_xy, d_yz, d_zx) lowered by -0.4 Δ_o (-4 Dq).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
OCTAHEDRAL CRYSTAL FIELD SPLITTING ($\Delta_o$)
                        
                                       e_g Doublet ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}$)
                                      ┌───┬───┐  ──► $+0.6 \Delta_o$ ($+6 Dq$)
                                      └───┴───┘
                                          ▲
   Degenerate 5 d-orbitals                │ $\Delta_o$ (Octahedral Splitting Energy)
   ┌───┬───┬───┬───┬───┐                  ▼
   └───┴───┴───┴───┴───┘              ┌───┬───┬───┐
                                      └───┴───┴───┘ ──► $-0.4 \Delta_o$ ($-4 Dq$)
                                       t_{2g} Triplet ($d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{zx}$)
conceptBreakdown.content:
In an Octahedral Ligand Field, ligands approach along Cartesian axes ($x, y, z$).
- **$e_g$ Set ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}$)**: Lobes point directly at incoming ligands $\rightarrow$ raised by $+0.6\Delta_o$.
- **$t_{2g}$ Set ($d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{zx}$)**: Lobes lie between axes $\rightarrow$ lowered by $-0.4\Delta_o$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Tetrahedral Crystal Field Splitting (Δ_t)
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Tetrahedral Crystal Field Splitting (Δ_t)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TETRAHEDRAL CRYSTAL FIELD SPLITTING (Δ_t)

• t₂ Set (d_xy, d_yz, d_zx): Raised by +0.4 Δ_t
• e Set (d_x²-y², d_z²):   Lowered by -0.6 Δ_t

Relationship: Δ_t = (4/9) Δ_o

High-Spin Rule: Because Δ_t is always much smaller than the Pairing Energy (Δ_t << P), Tetrahedral complexes are almost ALWAYS High-Spin!
conceptBreakdown.content:
In a Tetrahedral Field, four ligands approach between axes. The energy splitting is inverted and smaller:
$$\mathbf{\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9} \Delta_o}$$
Because $\Delta_t \ll P$, tetrahedral complexes are almost always high-spin.

quickRevision: Octahedral: e_g is raised by +0.6 Δ_o; t_2g is lowered by -0.4 Δ_o.
Tetrahedral: t_2 is raised by +0.4 Δ_t; e is lowered by -0.6 Δ_t.
Tetrahedral complexes are almost always high-spin because Δ_t << P.
